 Judgment
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.)No.149/2013 on the file of the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-I, Kottayam is the appellant herein.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents in the O.P. are the respondents herein.

The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 19.02.2012.

2. According to the petitioner, on 19.02.2012 at 12.10 p.m., while they were travelling in a car bearing No.KL-02X/3600 through the Kottayam-Kumarakom road and when the vehicle reached near Kannadichal junction, the driver of the car lost his control over the same and thereby it hit on another car bearing No.KL-05C/4635 which came from the opposite direction and as a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.8,20,000/- limited to Rs.6,00,000/-.
3. The 1st and 2nd respondents remained ex-parte.
The 2025:KER:15311 MACA NO. 452 OF 2016 3rd insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the other car.
4. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of RW1 and RW2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A12 and B1 to B8 and X1.

5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,56,055/- rounded off to 1,56,100/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.
7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:

sentences.text: Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

8. Heard Sri.P.M.Joshi, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri.A.R.George,
learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
2025:KER:15311 MACA NO. 452 OF 2016 9.
(c) Pain over thigh.
10. As per Ext.X1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, his permanent physical disability of the petitioner was assessed as 12%.

However, the tribunal has scaled down the same to 8%,
without assigning valid and cogent reasons.

The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.(See Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305).
Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 12%.
11. Another contention raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that, the notional income of the petitioner fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.4,000/- is on the lower side.
According to him, the 2025:KER:15311 MACA NO. 452 OF 2016 petitioner was a degree student, earning Rs.6000/- per month from tuition.
However, the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.4000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

12. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a Coolie, in the year 2012 will come to Rs.8,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the petitioner could not prove his job or income as claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra) , his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.8500/-.
13.
On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 22 years.

Therefore, 40 % of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: According to the learned counsel, the compensation 2025:KER:15311 MACA NO. 452 OF 2016 awarded on the heads pain and suffering, loss of amenities, extra nourishment are on the lower side.
He also submitted that, he has loss of education and nothing was awarded by the Tribunal.
In this case, the petitioner was treated as impatient for 30 days.
He also sustained very serious injuries in the accident, including five fractures.

In the said circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded on the heads pain and suffering, loss of amenities, extra nourishment are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.75,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.10,000/- respectively.
15.
For the same reasons, he is also entitled to get compensation for loss of education at least for a period of three months, which will come to Rs.25,500/- (Rs.8,500/- x 3).
16. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
17. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,73,883/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.
